To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: So this happened. Fernhollow Photo is officially a thing!!

I've started this post about six times, which is funny because usually I can tell you people about a dog stealing bread without needing a whole writing process. Apparently telling your family you started a business is a little different.

So. I started a business!! Fernhollow Photo LLC is real, the website is live, and I am officially going out on my own as a wedding photographer. With my own name on the emails and everything. Extremely normal, not at all terrifying.

I wanted to tell you here before Thanksgiving because I would like to eat Aunt Ruthie's turkey without making a major life announcement while somebody is passing me the gravy. Also this way I get to finish my sentences before Dad asks about health insurance.

Dad: I have health insurance sorted. I picked a marketplace plan, and it starts January 1. This paragraph is specifically for you. You can print it out and put it on the fridge.

The other part of this news is that Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and after four years shooting for her, that was a lot to take in. It's strange having something that was such a huge part of your life suddenly become the place you used to work. I still catch myself thinking about next season in terms of “we” and then remembering that the we looks different now.

I don't think I can explain what those four years meant without getting embarrassingly mushy about Marisol, so we're just going to do that for a minute. She basically taught me everything. Not just how to make a beautiful picture, but how to keep doing the job when the schedule has gone sideways and everybody is looking at you like you might somehow know where the missing boutonniere is.

She trusted me with more and more, and she made me a better photographer. Getting to work with her for four years was a very lucky thing. Marisol, if you read this, thank you. I will probably say that another hundred times.

And no, this wasn't a decision I made in a panic one afternoon in October. I've been planning some version of this in my head for two years. I just apparently needed another several hundred imaginary conversations with myself before I was ready to do it.

The actual LLC filing happened on October 22, on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. Very glamorous business headquarters. I finished it and cried a little, then had to pull myself together because I was still in a Fred Meyer parking lot and had other things to do.

I feel like somebody should give you a little certificate for that part. Not the LLC part. The having a big emotional moment and then continuing with your errands part.

Here's the part that makes me feel a lot less like I'm just standing in a parking lot making questionable choices: I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. FOURTEEN. Six came through Marisol's referrals, which means so much to me, and eight found me on my own. There are actual couples who have looked at my work and said, yes, that's who we want there.

I know that's literally how booking a photographer works. It still feels pretty amazing when the photographer is you.

The first booking that was completely mine was Dahlia and Ken. They're getting married at Timberline on June 12, and they found me because of the pictures I took of one of Marisol's couples at Multnomah Falls. Those photos went out into the world and somehow came back as an email from two people who wanted to hire Fernhollow Photo. I may be a little ridiculous about that wedding forever. Sorry in advance.

June is already my busiest month, with four weddings, and there's a Wallowa Lake wedding in September. My knees would like to be consulted about all of this. Their concerns have been noted.

Jae will be second shooting the big weddings with me, paid per wedding. So going out on my own does not mean I'm trying to be in two places at once while carrying every camera I own. I've worked enough weddings to know when I need another person.

Am I scared? Yes, obviously. I can be very confident about where you should stand for nice light and still get nervous about having an LLC. Those are apparently separate skills.

But I have bookings, I've been working through the numbers, and I've had two years to think about what I want this to look like. I'm not assuming every month will be easy. I am taking it seriously. Underneath the nerves, I'm really, really excited.

Also, the name. Grandma, this part is for you.

Fernhollow is from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I kept coming back to that when I was trying to name the business. Before there were wedding timelines and contracts and a camera bag that has permanently changed the shape of my shoulder, there was that trail and your camera.

So the name is for you. I wanted you to know that.

Sam celebrated by making a cake that said FERNHOLOW. One L short, otherwise a very professional launch event. We ate it anyway. I don't think the state of Oregon needs to hear about the spelling discrepancy.

Mom, yes, Sam is coming to Thanksgiving. We're bringing rolls and the cranberry thing, and I'll bring my camera too. Does anybody want free family pictures while we're all together? We can sneak outside before dinner. No pressure, but if you were already planning to ask me while I had a mouthful of stuffing, here's your chance to get ahead of it.

I'm so happy I finally get to tell you all. Please be excited with me. This is a big, scary, good thing, and I've wanted it for a long time.

Love you guys. See you at Ruthie's.

Dad, the insurance paragraph is near the top.
